data.narrative:
Ricursive Intelligence, a Series A-stage chip design company founded by Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini, operates within the Chips & Semiconductors sector alongside a comparables universe of 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage companies including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the company's $335M total raised as a proxy for implied valuation, application of a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $670M. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-peer datapoints within the same valuation tier and stage (only 2 datapoints available against a 3-minimum threshold). Public-comp anchoring using the Semiconductors sector P/S median of 21.5x could not be applied absent the target's disclosed revenue.

Given the single-method reliance, the triangulated valuation range is necessarily narrow: $570M (low), $670M (median), and $770M (high). This range reflects order-of-magnitude consistency around the stage-progression result, with bounds capturing modeling uncertainty. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data (limiting multiple-method validation), a sparse private peer set at this stage and valuation tier, and the company's early maturity within a capital-intensive sector. Investors should treat this range as preliminary pending additional financial and competitive disclosure.
